facts_of_case: The appellants are the legal representatives of defendant No.6. The plaintiff and defendants 1 and 2 are the children of Kumaran Vaidyar and Janaki. Defendants 5 to 9 are the legal representatives of the first defendant. Defendants 3 and 4 are the legal representatives of the second defendant.

legal_principles.principle: Property of a female Hindu to be her absolute property.
legal_principles.held: Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be held by her as full owner thereof and not as a limited owner.

legal_principles.principle: Sub-section (1) of Section 14 is large in its amplitude and covers every kind of acquisition of property by a female Hindu.
legal_principles.held: It will, therefore, be seen that sub-sec.(1) of Section 14 is large in its amplitude and covers every kind of acquisition of property by a female Hindu including acquisition in lieu of maintenance and where such property was possessed by her at the date of commencement of the Act or was subsequently acquired and possessed, she would become the full owner of the property.
cited_cases: Vaddeboyina Tulasamma and others v. Vaddeboyina Sesha Reddi

legal_principles.principle: Section 14(2) is more in the nature of a proviso or exception to sub-section (1).
legal_principles.held: Sub-section (2) must, therefore, be read in the context of sub-section (1) so as to leave as large a scope for operation as possible to sub-section (1) and so read, it must be confined to cases where property is acquired by a female Hindu for the first time as a grant without any pre-existing right, under a gift, will, instrument, decree, order or award, the terms of which prescribe a restricted estate in the property.
cited_cases: Vaddeboyina Tulasamma and others v. Vaddeboyina Sesha Reddi

outcome.final_order: The donee is entitled to claim the protection under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act.
